subject: Calculate a map when linkage groups and orders are known

messages.author: 13b6ace5063d6653
messages.subject: Calculate a map when linkage groups and orders are known
parts:
Hi Karl,

I have a dataset (SSD lines, GBS data) for which I already know the linkage groups and the order of the markers. I'd like to use R/qtl just to compute the maps of the linkage groups. Also, the dataset has some missing datapoints so this is why I want to use R/qtl, to calculate multipoint estimates of the recombination fractions.

How do I tell R/qtl to take the known orders from a file (or from a command line), then calculate the map for each linkage group, then returning the map to a file?

Do I need to use the argmax function prior to est.map, or does R/qtl calculates true multipoint on non-imputed data?

Note: I already have the datafile formatted for R/qtl.

Thanks a lot in advance for your advice,
Mathias

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Calculate a map when linkage groups and orders are known
parts:
> I have a dataset (SSD lines, GBS data) for which I already know the linkage groups and the order of the markers. I'd like to use R/qtl just to compute the maps of the linkage groups. Also, the dataset has some missing datapoints so this is why I want to use R/qtl, to calculate multipoint estimates of the recombination fractions.
>
> How do I tell R/qtl to take the known orders from a file (or from a command line), then calculate the map for each linkage group, then returning the map to a file?

If you create a CSV file with the genotypes, with markers as columns and lines as rows, use the 2nd row to indicate the linkage group identifiers. When imported into R with the read.cross() function, the order of the markers in the file is used as the order of markers along each linkage group. Arbitrary locations are assigned, or you can use a third row to give your own initial estimates of positions.

Then use est.map to estimate the inter-marker distances; it takes the marker order as truth.
> Do I need to use the argmax function prior to est.map, or does R/qtl calculates true multipoint on non-imputed data?

Don't try to impute missing data. R/qtl uses a hidden Markov model to derive multipoint estimates and can deal with the missing data.

karl
